title: Temporally-Resolved Token Attribution Reveals the Generation Dynamics of Diffusion Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.01177v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This work presents Diffusion Layer Integrated Gradients (DLIG), a token attribution method for diffusion language models (DLMs) that extends Integrated Gradients (IG~\cite{sundararajan2017axiomatic}) to arbitrary layers and denoising steps. DLIG attributes a DLM's progressive commitment to a self-generated or fixed completion for an input prompt. We establish direct correspondences between DLIG and the IG axioms of completeness, implementation invariance, linearity, and symmetry preservation. As a lightweight complement to interventional analysis, DLIG provides an inexpensive first check of mechanistic hypotheses across the denoising trajectory. We demonstrate this on word-sense disambiguation, multi-hop graph reasoning, and sentence infilling, revealing how DLMs draw on inputs across positions, layers, and denoising steps.

translated_title: 时间分辨的词元归因揭示扩散语言模型的生成动态
translated_abstract: 本工作提出了扩散层积分梯度（DLIG），这是一种针对扩散语言模型（DLM）的词元归因方法，将积分梯度（IG）扩展到任意层和去噪步骤。DLIG对DLM在输入提示下对自生成或固定补全的渐进承诺进行归因。我们建立了DLIG与IG公理（完备性、实现不变性、线性性和对称性保持）之间的直接对应关系。作为干预分析的轻量级补充，DLIG在整个去噪轨迹上提供了一种低成本的机制假设初步检验方法。我们在词义消歧、多跳图推理和句子填充任务上验证了该方法，揭示了DLM如何在不同位置、层和去噪步骤上利用输入信息。
tldr: 本文提出DLIG方法，将积分梯度扩展到扩散语言模型的任意层和去噪步骤，实现时间分辨的词元归因，以低成本揭示模型在整个去噪轨迹中如何利用输入信息进行生成。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes DLIG, a token attribution method that extends Integrated Gradients to arbitrary layers and denoising steps of diffusion language models, enabling inexpensive temporally-resolved analysis of how DLMs draw on inputs across the denoising trajectory.
